newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes gain slightly in modest Aug action.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes gain slightly in modest Aug action.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf rose slightly Wednesday morning in tight trading ranges, while August grades stumbled to mixed results.

September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was nearly 10 cents higher at $19.50-60 a barrel, tracking NYMEX movement. August/September spreads were sold as wide as minus 30 cents, and have also moved at -26 and -25 cents, putting outright August benchmark around $19.20-30 a barrel.
Grade barrels moved in sluggish volumes, with deals seen for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 15 cts and 19 cts over the marker, and for West Texas Sour/Midland at -$1.45, traders said.
August grade business was called surprisingly quiet by brokers, who noted that pipeline scheduling day lies ahead on Friday.
"It looks like there is a tight lid on things out there, maybe showing that most refiners completed their business already," said a cash dealer in Texas.
Market news focused on reports Cano Limon crude loadings in Colombia are being delayed 10-20 days under new July and August schedules arranged after pipeline closings.

Leftist rebel attacks crippled the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline from July 6 until last week, resulting in force majeure declarations by Cano Limon field operator Occidental Petroleum Corp and by state oil company Ecopetrol.
